caption: Heat rises from a barbecue grill on a summer afternoon, and the view of the fence behind it wavers in the shimmering air.

sa.check: The air above the grill shimmers.
The fence behind wavers where it is seen through the shimmer.
The shimmer is strongest just above the grill.
The fence stands steady where it is not seen through the shimmer.

pc.expect: The shimmer rises from the grill and fades with height; it does not flow downward.
pc.fail: The shimmer flows down the grill's sides and pools on the ground; or sinks below the grill; or pours downward through the grill's bars; or hangs as a fixed band without rising.

pc.expect: The shimmer keeps rising while the grill is hot and the wavering keeps moving upward, easing as the grill cools.
pc.fail: The shimmer runs back down into the grill; or the wavering freezes into a fixed pattern; or the shimmer thickens steadily long after the fire is out; or a waver retreats toward the grill.

pc.expect: Only the part of the fence seen through the rising air wavers and the rest stands steady.
pc.fail: The whole fence wavers including parts seen well away from the shimmer; or the fence stands perfectly steady behind a strong shimmer; or the shimmer sits over a cold part of the yard while the air above the grill is still.

pc.expect: The grill and the fence stay put; only the air above the grill moves.
pc.fail: The fence's boards shift or lean; or the grill slides with nothing touching it; or the grill's lid swings by itself; or objects beside the grill jump.

pc.expect: One grill and one fence; the fence keeps its boards and the grill its parts.
pc.fail: A fence board vanishes; or a new board appears; or the grill's lid vanishes; or the fence changes into a wall.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The fence's colour, the grill's body and the yard stay the same.
pc.fail: The fence changes colour; or the grill changes colour; or items in the yard rearrange.
